key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset after head trauma. LOCATION: GENERALIZED symptoms. DURATION: Symptoms may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: HEADACHE, dizziness, confusion. AGGRAVATING: LIGHT, sound, movement, cognitive tasks. RELIEVING: REST, avoiding triggers. TIMING: Immediate onset after trauma, may persist for days to weeks. SEVERITY: 4-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: HEADACHE, dizziness, confusion, memory problems, nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light and sound. KEY POSITIVES: Headache, dizziness, confusion, memory problems, sensitivity to light and sound. KEY NEGATIVES: No focal neurological deficits, no signs of increased intracranial pressure.

red_flags: Severe headache with vomiting - possible intracranial hemorrhage, call 911
Altered mental status with focal neurological deficits - possible traumatic brain injury, call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
